answer: Layered quorums: no single jury settles an answer. A grade must hold at the vertex of three independent panels drawn separately, each seeing only the text, so one corrupted panel cannot push junk through - it would need collusion across a canyon of isolated draws. Disagreement between panels triggers a fresh draw rather than a tiebreak, so attackers cannot even learn which jurors to target. A pearl forms as irritants accrue layer by layer; so does trust here, each sealed round adding another coat. A sybil must win three unconnected lotteries per answer, at rising odds against.
